questions.question: Length of a train is 330 metres and it is moving at the speed of 72 km/hr. In how much time will it takes cross a platform of length 710 metres ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Distance to be covered = Length of Train + Length of Platform = 330 + 710 = 1040 m.

Speed in m/s = 72 × 5/18 = 20 m/s.

Time Taken = Total Distance ÷ Speed = 1040 ÷ 20 = 52 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 52 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of Train (L₁) = 330 m

Length of Platform (L₂) = 710 m

Speed of Train (v) = 72 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Time = Total Distance ÷ Speed

Total Distance = Length of Train + Length of Platform

Speed in m/s = Speed in km/hr × (5/18)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7e9af6861dafb67b8adb1fd27fa47579a3c79dfc16bd016c04bf0c97f9bcab90.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Convert speed from km/hr to m/s:

⇒ Speed = 72 × (5/18) m/s

⇒ Speed = 4 × 5 = 20 m/s

⇒ Total Distance = 330 + 710 = 1040 m

⇒ Time taken = 1040 ÷ 20

⇒ Time taken = 52 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 52 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Crossing Stationary Objects

When a train crosses a stationary object of negligible length (pole, man), distance = length of train. When it crosses an object of length L (platform, bridge, tunnel), distance = length of train + L.

Relative Speed

If two objects move in the same direction, relative speed = |u − v|. If they move in opposite directions, relative speed = u + v.</p

questions.question: Vinay and Mahesh are 250 metres apart from each other. They are moving towards each other with the speed of 36 km/hr and 54 km hr respectively. In how much time will they meet each other ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction) = Sum of Speeds = 36 + 54 = 90 km/hr.

Convert Speed to m/s = 90 × (5/18) = 25 m/s.

Meeting Time = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed = 250 ÷ 25 = 10 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance between Vinay and Mahesh = 250 m

Speed of Vinay (S₁) = 36 km/hr

Speed of Mahesh (S₂) = 54 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction) = S₁ + S₂

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3870e8c6f0ff44a42f1db3e3c0766b060118e0041fb6092ac73dc3ba21709682.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Speed in km/hr = 36 + 54 = 90 km/hr

⇒ Conversion to m/s: Speed × (5/18)

⇒ Relative Speed (Sᵣₑₗ) = 90 × (5/18) = 5 × 5 = 25 m/s

⇒ Time (T) = Distance (D) ÷ Sᵣₑₗ

⇒ T = 250 ÷ 25

⇒ T = 10 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 10 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Cases

When moving in opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂. When moving in the same direction, relative speed = S₁ − S₂ (where S₁ > S₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Meeting Time Formula

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed. This is applicable whether objects move towards each other or one chases another.</p

questions.question: A student goes to school at a speed of 5(1)/(2) km/h and returns at a speed of 4 km/h. If he takes 4(3)/(4) hours for the entire journey, then the total distance covered by the student (in km) is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total distance = Average Speed × Total Time

Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) / (S₁ + S₂)

S₁ = 5.5 km/h, S₂ = 4 km/h, Time = 4.75 hours

Average Speed = (2 × 5.5 × 4) / (5.5 + 4) = 44 / 9.5 = 88 / 19 km/h

Total Distance = (88 / 19) × 4.75 = (88 / 19) × (19 / 4) = 22 km

**∴ The correct answer is 22 km.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed while going (S₁) = 5½ km/h = 11/2 km/h = 5.5 km/h

Speed while returning (S₂) = 4 km/h

Total time taken (T) = 4¾ hours = 19/4 hours = 4.75 hours

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/82175b73e1c3faf911a437a9403c2348ea9a0057f5a43bb12b96f3a06f6fe8df.png] 

**Calculation:**

Let the distance between the student’s home and school be D km.

⇒ Time taken to go = Distance ÷ Speed = D / 5.5 = 2D/11 hours

⇒ Time taken to return = Distance ÷ Speed = D / 4 hours

⇒ Total Time = Time to go + Time to return

⇒ 2D/11 + D/4 = 19/4

⇒ (8D + 11D) / 44 = 19/4

⇒ 19D / 44 = 19/4

⇒ D / 44 = 1/4

⇒ D = 44 / 4 = 11 km

⇒ Total distance covered = One-way distance × 2

⇒ Total distance = 11 × 2 = 22 km

**∴ The correct answer is 22 km.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Distance

When an object covers equal distances at different speeds S₁ and S₂, the average speed is (2 × S₁ × S₂) / (S₁ + S₂).

Distance Formula for Total Time

One-way distance D = [ (S₁ × S₂) / (S₁ + S₂) ] × Total Time taken for the round trip.

Speed-Time Relation

For a constant distance, speed is inversely proportional to time (S ∝ 1/T). Therefore, S₁/S₂ = T₂/T₁.</p

questions.question: A plane flies a distance of 1800 km in 5 hours. What is its average speed in meters/second?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed in km/h = 1800 ÷ 5 = 360 km/h

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18.

Speed in m/s = 360 × (5/18) = 20 × 5 = 100 m/s.

**∴ The correct answer is 100 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Distance = 1800 km

Total Time = 5 hours

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Conversion Factor: 1 km/h = (5/18) m/s

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fe367f49553c92ee4298e7340733be7c6b8cb3219744113cd743871b17d2a1eb.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Average Speed (in km/h) = 1800 ÷ 5

⇒ Average Speed = 360 km/h

⇒ Conversion to m/s: 360 × (1000 m / 3600 s)

⇒ Average Speed = 360 × (5/18) m/s

⇒ Average Speed = 20 × 5 m/s

⇒ Average Speed = 100 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 100 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion Rules

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed for Two Parts

If a journey is divided into two equal distances with speeds v₁ and v₂, the average speed = (2 × v₁ × v₂) ÷ (v₁ + v₂).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed is the difference (u − v). In opposite directions, it is the sum (u + v).</p

questions.question: Two runners A and B start running at 12 km/hr and 16 km/hr towards each other. They meet after 1 hour and 30 minutes. How far (in km) were they from each other when they started?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative Speed (towards each other) = Speed A + Speed B = 12 + 16 = 28 km/hr.

Time = 1 hour 30 minutes = 1.5 hours.

Initial Distance = Relative Speed × Time.

Distance = 28 × 1.5 = 42 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 42 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of runner A (SA) = 12 km/hr

Speed of runner B (SB) = 16 km/hr

Meeting time (T) = 1 hour 30 minutes

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0d66f3f355590009c64ff7474b4c3142fe008a3fc5a241b1cd6e5b4102740d71.png] 

**Formula:**

Total Distance = (Relative Speed) × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time in hours = 1 + 30/60 = 1.5 hours

⇒ Relative Speed (Opposite Direction) = SA + SB

⇒ Relative Speed = 12 + 16 = 28 km/hr

⇒ Distance = 28 × 1.5

⇒ Distance = 28 × 3/2

⇒ Distance = 14 × 3 = 42 km

**∴ The correct answer is 42 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move towards each other, relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂). If they move in the same direction, it is the difference (S₁ − S₂).

Distance-Speed-Time Relation

The basic formula is Distance = Speed × Time. To find time, use Time = Distance ÷ Speed.

Unit Conversion

Always ensure units are consistent. To convert minutes to hours, divide by 60. To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18.</p

questions.question: Train A takes 1 hour more than train B to travel a distance of 720 km. Due to engine trouble speed of train B falls by one third, so it takes 3 hours more than Train A to complete the same journey. What is the speed of Train A (in km/hr)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed ratio for Train B = 1 : (1 − 1/3) = 1 : 2/3 = 3 : 2

Time ratio for Train B = 2 : 3 (Inverse of speed ratio as distance is constant)

Difference in B's time = 3 − 2 = 1 unit

Actual time difference for B = (Time A + 3) − (Time A − 1) = 4 hours

∴ 1 unit = 4 hours → Original time of B = 2 × 4 = 8 hours

Time taken by Train A = 8 + 1 = 9 hours → Speed A = 720 ÷ 9 = 80 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 80 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Distance = 720 km. Train A time = Train B time + 1 hr. After speed reduction of 1/3, New Train B time = Train A time + 3 hr.

**Formula Used:** Time = Distance ÷ Speed | Speed ∝ 1/Time (when distance is constant)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bda80b7926495bc44266bf611c762fd19b28000677446d03bde4eacabc93121c.png] 

Let original speed and time of Train B be Sb and Tb respectively.

⇒ Tₐ = Tb + 1 --- (Eq. 1)

⇒ New Speed of B = Sb − (1/3)Sb = 2/3 Sb

⇒ New Time of B (Tb') = Distance ÷ (2/3 Sb) = 3/2 (Distance ÷ Sb) = 3/2 Tb

⇒ Tb' = Tₐ + 3 --- (Eq. 2)

Substitute Tₐ from Eq. 1 into Eq. 2:

⇒ 3/2 Tb = (Tb + 1) + 3

⇒ 3/2 Tb − Tb = 4

⇒ 1/2 Tb = 4

⇒ Tb = 8 hours

⇒ Tₐ = 8 + 1 = 9 hours

⇒ Speed of Train A = Distance ÷ Tₐ = 720 ÷ 9

⇒ Speed of Train A = 80 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 80 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Relationship of Speed and Time

When the distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S₁/S₂ = T₂/T₁). This allows solving complex speed problems using simple ratios.

Average Speed Formula

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. For two equal distances with speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy/(x + y).

Unit Conversions

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: A car travelling at an average speed of 72 km/hr takes 9 minutes to travel a certain distance. By how much should it increase its speed (in km/hr) to travel the same distance in 8 minutes?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For a constant distance, Speed is inversely proportional to Time (S ∝ 1/T).

Ratio of Time = 9 : 8

Ratio of Speed = 8 : 9

Initial Speed (8 units) = 72 km/hr ⇒ 1 unit = 9 km/hr

Increase in speed = 9 − 8 = 1 unit = 9 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 9 km/hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Speed (S₁) = 72 km/hr

Initial Time (T₁) = 9 minutes = 9/60 hours

New Time (T₂) = 8 minutes = 8/60 hours

**Formula:** Distance = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dad09fccde22a4c8ca24a5f41d7be4c1c0019bdcf646f9907e64f9df97b13115.png] 

⇒ Distance = S₁ × T₁

⇒ Distance = 72 × (9/60) = 10.8 km

⇒ New Speed (S₂) = Distance ÷ T₂

⇒ S₂ = 10.8 ÷ (8/60) = (10.8 × 60) ÷ 8

⇒ S₂ = 648 ÷ 8 = 81 km/hr

⇒ Increase in speed = S₂ − S₁

⇒ Increase in speed = 81 − 72 = 9 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 9 km/hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relationship between Speed, Distance, and Time

When distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S₁ × T₁ = S₂ × T₂). If distance varies, then Distance ∝ Speed × Time.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5. To convert minutes to hours, divide by 60.

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. For two equal distances covered at speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).</p

questions.question: If a boat goes upstream at a speed of 24 km/hr and comes back the same distance at 40 km/hr. What is the average speed (in km/hr) for the total journey?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the distance traveled is the same for both parts of the journey, use the harmonic mean formula.

Average Speed = (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y)

Where x = 24 km/hr and y = 40 km/hr.

Average Speed = (2 × 24 × 40) ÷ (24 + 40) = 1920 ÷ 64 = 30 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Upstream Speed (u) = 24 km/hr

Downstream Speed (v) = 40 km/hr

Formula: Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/70e63365e330d85a0d9ecd89dbdf2618bc8bc4bf2b3c67b78ffd683dd9a2a4d1.png] 

⇒ Let the distance between the two points be the LCM of 24 and 40.

⇒ LCM(24, 40) = 120 km.

⇒ Time taken while going upstream (t₁) = 120 ÷ 24 = 5 hours.

⇒ Time taken while coming back downstream (t₂) = 120 ÷ 40 = 3 hours.

⇒ Total Distance = 120 + 120 = 240 km.

⇒ Total Time = 5 + 3 = 8 hours.

⇒ Average Speed = 240 ÷ 8 = 30 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed of Boat in Still Water

It is the average of downstream and upstream speeds: Speedbₒₐₜ = (Downstream + Upstream) ÷ 2.

Speed of the Stream (Current)

It is half the difference between downstream and upstream speeds: Speedₛₜᵣₑₐₘ = (Downstream − Upstream) ÷ 2.

General Average Speed

For unequal distances, Average Speed = (d₁ + d₂ + ... + dₙ) ÷ (t₁ + t₂ + ... + tₙ).</p

questions.question: Excluding stoppages, the speed of a bus is 80 kmph and including stoppages, it is 60 kmph. For how many minutes does the bus stop per hour?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15**__
**__Key Points__**
__

• The speed of the bus **excluding stoppages** is **80 kmph**. This implies that in one hour of continuous running, the bus covers **80 kilometers**.

• The speed of the bus **including stoppages** is **60 kmph**. This means that in one actual hour (including stop time), the bus covers only **60 kilometers**.

• The **reduction in distance** covered in one hour due to stops is: 80 − 60 = **20 km**.

• The **stop time** is equivalent to the time the bus would have taken to cover those **20 km** if it had been running at its non-stop speed of **80 kmph**.

• Using the formula: **Time = Distance ÷ Speed**.

• Stoppage time in hours = 20 ÷ 80 = **1/4 hour**.

• To convert hours into minutes: 1/4 × 60 = **15 minutes**.

• Therefore, the bus stops for **15 minutes** every hour.

**Additional Information__**

• A quick **shortcut formula** for this type of problem is: **Stop time per hour = (Faster Speed − Slower Speed) ÷ Faster Speed**.

• Applying the formula: (80 − 60) ÷ 80 = 20 ÷ 80 = 1/4 hour. Multiply by 60 to get **15 minutes**.

• This logic is based on the fact that the **deficit in distance** is entirely due to the time spent at **stoppages**, during which the bus is not moving at its **constant speed**.

• Understanding the difference between **Average Speed** and **Instantaneous Speed** is crucial in solving **Time, Speed, and Distance** problems.
</ul

questions.question: Flight A usually takes 1 hour more than Flight B to travel a distance of 7200 km. Due to engine trouble, the speed of flight B becomes 5/6 times of its actual speed, so it takes 36 minutes more than Flight A to complete the same journey. What is the speed of Flight A (in km/hr)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed ratio of B = 1 : 5/6 = 6 : 5

Time ratio of B = 5 : 6 (since distance is constant)

Difference in B's time = 1 unit = 1 hour (initial lead) + 0.6 hours (later lag) = 1.6 hours

Original time of Flight B = 5 units = 5 × 1.6 = 8 hours

Usual time of Flight A = 8 + 1 = 9 hours

Speed of Flight A = 7200 ÷ 9 = 800 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 800 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Distance = 7200 km

Usual Time difference: TA − TB = 1 hour

New speed of B = 5/6 × Original speed of B

New time difference: T'B − TA = 36/60 hours = 0.6 hours

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d0aaad0e4c9ddc8f15213adb19d4e51d16659fce3e500ea87784dd4e19f29977.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

When distance is constant, Speed₁ × Time₁ = Speed₂ × Time₂

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total change in time for Flight B = (TA + 0.6) − (TA − 1)

⇒ Total change in time for Flight B = 1.6 hours

⇒ Let usual time for B be TB. New time T'B = (6/5) × TB

⇒ T'B − TB = 1.6

⇒ (6/5)TB − TB = 1.6

⇒ (1/5)TB = 1.6

⇒ TB = 1.6 × 5 = 8 hours

⇒ Usual time of Flight A = TB + 1 = 8 + 1 = 9 hours

⇒ Speed of Flight A = 7200 ÷ 9

⇒ Speed of Flight A = 800 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 800 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed-Time Relationship

For a fixed distance, speed is inversely proportional to time. If speed becomes x/y of original, time becomes y/x of original.

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed is the difference between their speeds (S₁ − S₂).

Average Speed

If a journey is divided into two equal distances with speeds x and y, the average speed is 2xy ÷ (x + y).</p
